scope_note: Every cell class, ctr included. A dense-contraction cell carries its caller-declared role hints in `contraction` (M/N/K as operand axes {operand, axis}, batch axes as iteration-frame axes, weight and scale as call-order operand slots); contraction_declared is true iff `contraction` is non-null. `expected` is reference output; only vectors carrying `spec_golden` reproduce an Appendix A.1 token whose bytes were hand-derived in the spec text. A second deriver cross-checks the rest.
cell_note: operands are listed in CALL order. The canonical order (§6.6-0014: inputs and in-place operands in call order, then outputs) is the CALLER's presentation (§6.6-0012); this reference reorders as a convenience, and a deriver whose input contract is canonical order reports NOT-EXPRESSIBLE on vector call_order_is_not_canonical_order, which is not a defect. reduced_axes are frame axes, 0 = outermost; index_operand is a call-order slot. accumulator null = the compute dtype.

vectors.name: a1_binary_add
vectors.note: the canonical derivation golden: two inputs + output, contiguous f32 [128,256]

vectors.name: a1_binary_add_operand1_broadcast_axis0
vectors.note: operand 1 stride [0,1]: layout br, mask 01, v1

vectors.name: a1_reduction_trailing_axis
vectors.note: keepdim [4,8]->[4,1]: rlast; output mask 02 (extent-1 axis, frame extent 8)

vectors.name: a1_reduction_all_axes
vectors.note: keepdim [4,8]->[1,1]: rall; output mask 03

vectors.name: a1_reduction_rank1
vectors.note: rank-1 [8]->[1]: all-axes AND trailing; rall wins the tie

vectors.name: a1_reduction_subset_rank4
vectors.note: [2,4,3,5]->[2,1,3,1] reducing axes 1 and 3: bitmask x0a; output mask 0a

vectors.name: a1_reduction_f16_accumulates_f32
vectors.note: accumulator f32 != compute f16: |f32/st carried

vectors.name: a1_inplace_accumulate
vectors.note: an in-place operand appears once, as an input; n_operands = 2

vectors.name: call_order_is_not_canonical_order
vectors.note: the output listed FIRST in call order: this reference canonicalizes (a convenience — the caller's job per §6.6-0012) and yields the a1_binary_add token; a deriver that takes canonical order reports NOT-EXPRESSIBLE here

vectors.name: lower_rank_operand_in_frame
vectors.note: operand 1 rank 1 [256] in frame [128,256]: mask over the padded view (01), layout/vec/div from its OWN axes (co, v4, d16)

vectors.name: extent1_axis_with_nonzero_stride
vectors.note: operand 1 [1,256] recording stride 256 on the unit axis: same tensor, same sub-key as the [0,1] broadcast view (#520)

vectors.name: extent1_axis_with_zero_stride
vectors.note: operand 1 [1,256] recording stride 0: byte-identical to extent1_axis_with_nonzero_stride

vectors.name: flipped_inner_axis
vectors.note: operand 1 inner stride -1: flipped flag r, v1 (not a forward-unit run); layout uses |stride| so it stays contiguous

vectors.name: strided_inner_axis
vectors.note: operand 1 strides [512,2]: layout st, v1

vectors.name: alignment_zero_derives_v1
vectors.note: alignment 0 cannot honor a packed load: v1 on every operand

vectors.name: innermost_axis_extent_one_is_axis_rank_minus_1
vectors.note: [4,1]: innermost active axis is axis 1 (extent 1: bucket da, width v1), not axis 0 (the clause's worked example)

vectors.name: innermost_axis_extent_eight_after_unit_axis
vectors.note: [1,8]: innermost active axis is axis 1 (extent 8: bucket d8) (the clause's worked example)

vectors.name: innermost_axis_extent_zero_is_axis_rank_minus_1
vectors.note: [8,0]: innermost active axis is axis 1 with E = 0: bucket da (6.5-0012 'covering ... E = 0'), NOT d8 from the outer axis

vectors.name: sub_byte_dtype_i4
vectors.note: i4 storage is under one byte: v1 whatever the alignment and extent

vectors.name: index_width_just_below_2_31
vectors.note: max touched offset 32768*65535 + 32767 = 2^31 - 1: ix32

vectors.name: index_width_at_2_31
vectors.note: max touched offset 32768*65536 + 32767 = 2^31 + 32767: ix64 (the boundary is exclusive)

vectors.name: work_class_32_is_warp
vectors.note: frame element count on the work-class boundary: <=32 warp, <=1024 block, else grid

vectors.name: work_class_1024_is_block
vectors.note: frame element count on the work-class boundary: <=32 warp, <=1024 block, else grid

vectors.name: work_class_1025_is_grid
vectors.note: frame element count on the work-class boundary: <=32 warp, <=1024 block, else grid

vectors.name: indexed_access_declared_index_slot
vectors.note: index slot declared: class ndx whatever the shapes

vectors.name: not_pointwise_output_narrower_than_frame
vectors.note: no declared fact, output [128,128] in frame [128,256]: oth

vectors.name: quantized_operand_dequant_form
vectors.note: operand 0 carries a quant record (linear): sixth sub-key component dl; the scale sibling carries none

vectors.name: reduction_f64_accumulator
vectors.note: accumulator f64 != compute f32: |f64/st

vectors.name: reduction_reduced_mantissa_only
vectors.note: accumulator == compute but <mp> rm: |f32/rm (both slots spelled)

vectors.name: ctr_gemm_small_m_large_nk
vectors.note: the §2.8(d) worked example: lhs [8,4096] . rhs [4096,4096] -> [8,4096]; M tiny, N and K large, K divisible by 16: ctll/d16, not batched. Roles are operand axes: frame axis 0 is max(8,4096,8), so the frame extent is NOT M

vectors.name: ctr_gemm_roles_swapped_m_and_n
vectors.note: the same operands as ctr_gemm_small_m_large_nk with the caller declaring M and N the other way round: the M/N classes follow the DECLARED axes (cl.. vs ct..), never the extents

vectors.name: ctr_k_divisibility_from_k_axis
vectors.note: K = 4100 (divisible by 4, not 8): d4, from the K axis and not from the innermost axis of the output (N = 4096 would give d16)

vectors.name: ctr_accumulator_and_reduced_mantissa
vectors.note: accumulator f32 != compute f16, <mp> rm: /f16/f32/f16/rm inside the contraction field; no separate (acc+mp) field (the two never coexist)

vectors.name: ctr_rank3_batch_not_declared
vectors.note: the same rank-3 operands with NO batch hint: not batched, the b coordinate is absent although the leading extent is 64

vectors.name: ctr_batch_declared_extent_one
vectors.note: a declared batch axis of extent 1 is batched (/bt): batched is a declaration, not an extent test

vectors.name: ctr_rank4_two_batch_axes_product
vectors.note: [4,64,8,512] . [4,64,512,4096]: batch axes 0 and 1 declared; the class is that of the PRODUCT 4*64 = 256 (/bm), not of either extent

vectors.name: ctr_rank4_one_batch_axis_declared
vectors.note: the same rank-4 operands, only axis 1 declared: class of 64 (/bs). The hint decides which axes count

vectors.name: ctr_rank4_no_batch_declared
vectors.note: the same rank-4 operands, no hint: a rank above 3 is not batched by rank alone

vectors.name: ctr_quantized_scale_e8m0
vectors.note: [activation, weight i4, scale f8e8m0]: weight slot 1, scale slot 2: /i4/bf16/bf16/st/qf8e8m0

vectors.name: ctr_quantized_scale_f16
vectors.note: the same cell with an f16 scale: a different key (/qf16), because the two scales decode the same stored values to different numbers

vectors.name: ctr_weight_second_undeclared_accumulator_defaults_to_operand0_dtype
vectors.note: [activation bf16, weight i4 (slot 1), scale], NO accumulator declared: <acc> is operand 0's dtype bf16 (/i4/bf16/bf16), NOT the weight's i4. Pairs with the weight-first vector, where operand 0 IS the weight (/i4/i4/bf16): the default follows operand 0, never the weight role

vectors.name: ctr_quantized_no_scale_designated
vectors.note: the same operands, no scale designated: the q coordinate is omitted, never empty

vectors.name: ctr_weight_role_not_operand_one
vectors.note: call order [weight i4, scale f8e8m0, activation]: the weight is operand 0 and a scale sits at position 1, so a positional operand-1 read names f8e8m0 where i4 is meant. Declared weight 0, scale 1, accumulator bf16

vectors.name: ctr_weight_first_undeclared_accumulator_defaults_to_operand0_dtype
vectors.note: the ctr_weight_role_not_operand_one operands with NO accumulator declared: <acc> defaults to the compute dtype = operand 0's dtype (here the weight, i4: /i4/i4/bf16). With the weight NOT at operand 0 (ctr_quantized_scale_e8m0, accumulator also undeclared) it is the operand-0 dtype bf16, not the weight's i4. Differs from the declared-bf16 vector in <acc> only

vectors.name: decline_ctr_axis_roles_not_distinct
vectors.note: K names the same operand axis as M

vectors.name: decline_ctr_axis_out_of_range
vectors.note: N names axis 5 of a rank-2 operand

vectors.name: decline_ctr_axis_operand_out_of_range

vectors.name: decline_ctr_weight_slot_out_of_range
vectors.note: the weight role names slot 7 of a 3-operand cell

vectors.name: decline_ctr_scale_slot_out_of_range
vectors.note: the scale role names slot 7 of a 3-operand cell: not silently ignored

vectors.name: decline_ctr_reserved_weight_dtype
vectors.note: the designated weight is a reserved dtype (f8e4m3fnuz): <wdt> is a key position, so unlike a sibling operand it declines

vectors.name: decline_ctr_no_output_operand
vectors.note: no output operand: <out> has no source

vectors.name: decline_ctr_batch_axis_out_of_range
vectors.note: batch axis 7 of a rank-3 frame

vectors.name: decline_ctr_batch_axis_duplicate
vectors.note: batch axis 0 listed twice

vectors.name: decline_ctr_batch_axis_is_an_mnk_axis
vectors.note: batch axis 1 is frame axis 1, which M occupies

vectors.name: decline_ctr_batch_axis_not_in_output
vectors.note: the output is rank 2 in a rank-3 frame: frame axis 0 is not an output axis

vectors.name: decline_ctr_batch_axis_zero_extent
vectors.note: a declared batch axis of extent 0 (every operand agrees): extent below 1

vectors.name: decline_scale_dtype_at_operand0
vectors.note: operand 0 is an MX scale dtype: no primary dtype, never 'the next operand'

vectors.name: decline_reserved_dtype
vectors.note: a reserved dtype (f8e4m3fnuz) at operand 0 — the key's dtype field (a KEY position): typed decline

vectors.name: reserved_dtype_at_non_primary_operand_derives
vectors.note: a reserved dtype (f8e6m2) at operand 1 is NOT a key position (§6.6-0015): the cell derives a token, no decline — two independent derivers (Fuel, Baracuda) agreed against the first draft of this corpus on exactly this

vectors.name: decline_collapsed_reduction_output
vectors.note: reduction output of rank 1 for a rank-2 frame: a collapsed output is rejected, not keyed

vectors.name: decline_reduced_axis_out_of_range
vectors.note: declared reduced axis 2 in a rank-2 frame

vectors.name: vec_cap_undeclared_is_16_bytes
vectors.note: f32 [64,128] on a target declaring no cap: 16 bytes, v4 (the control for the next two)

vectors.name: vec_cap_32_bytes_widens_f32_to_v8
vectors.note: same cell, target declares a 32-byte cap: 8*4 = 32 <= 32, v8 (differs from the 16-byte control in vec only)

vectors.name: vec_cap_8_bytes_narrows_f32_to_v2
vectors.note: same cell, target declares an 8-byte cap: 2*4 = 8 <= 8, v2

vectors.name: mx_f4e2m1_elementwise_add
vectors.note: an elementwise add on an MX element dtype: sub-byte storage never vectorizes, so every operand is v1; no accumulator coordinate is spelled

vectors.name: mx_f6e2m3_elementwise_add
vectors.note: an elementwise add on an MX element dtype: sub-byte storage never vectorizes, so every operand is v1; no accumulator coordinate is spelled

vectors.name: mx_f6e3m2_elementwise_add
vectors.note: an elementwise add on an MX element dtype: sub-byte storage never vectorizes, so every operand is v1; no accumulator coordinate is spelled

vectors.name: mx_f4e2m1_ctr_undeclared_accumulator_declines
vectors.note: a contraction whose operand 0 is f4e2m1 with no declared accumulator: <acc> would default to the compute dtype, an MX element, so the deriver declines

vectors.name: mx_f4e2m1_ctr_declared_accumulator_derives
vectors.note: the same contraction with accumulator f32 declared: <wdt> and <out> may be the MX element, so it derives
